children: has told the Ukrainian government that it cannot safely restart operations at its steelmaking unit in the country following a series of missile strikes.

The Luxembourg-based steelmaker expects to record an impairment charge of about $1B against its ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih subsidiary after four attacks over the past five weeks caused fatalities, injuries, and extensive damage, the company said Friday.
“It is with deep regret that we have concluded that we are no longer able to safely operate,” Mauro Longobardo, chief executive officer of ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih, said in a

. “We are discussing the future of the plant with the government of Ukraine and will focus on preserving the infrastructure, so when peace finally returns, options for restarting production remain available.”
ArcelorMittal said it has provided more than $700M to keep ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih operating since the start of the war.

Ukraine’s industrial infrastructure has come under intensified attacks in recent weeks, with Moscow threatening “massive strikes” against the country’s energy facilities in response to attacks by Kyiv on civilian and energy infrastructure.

title: ArcelorMittal unable to safely resume Ukraine operations after strikes
